To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the beneficial effect of a novel treatment on a composite primary endpoint may be a false positive result, which is due to a lack of power to detect the effect of the novel treatment on mortality, which is the only component that is relevant for patients.
the effect of a novel treatment on a composite morbidity endpoint is not a reliable surrogate for the effect on mortality.
the effect of a novel treatment on mortality and morbidity can be assessed using a simple method that is applicable to any clinical trial that reports a composite endpoint.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of statistical methodology for the analysis and interpretation of clinical trials that have a complex primary endpoint.
the interpretation of the results of contemporary clinical trials and how these results can be applied in clinical practice.
the interpretation of clinical trials and the implications for the design of future trials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment was beneficial for the morbidity component(s) that were shown to be beneficial, but that the effect on the mortality component was inconclusive.
a novel treatment has a beneficial effect on only a subset of morbidity components and an indeterminate effect for mortality.

the treatment has been demonstrated to reduce morbidity for the components that have been clearly demonstrated to benefit and to have an indeterminate effect for the other morbidity outcomes and mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect on morbidity is not necessarily an indicator of the effect on mortality.

a novel treatment may be beneficial for one or more morbidity components and not for others, but it is not clear whether the novel treatment is beneficial or harmful for mortality, and it is not clear how this effect on mortality may be balanced against the morbidity benefit.
the effect of a novel treatment on mortality is indeterminate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the potential for harm from a novel treatment is often overlooked in the excitement about a beneficial effect on one or two morbidity components.
a beneficial effect on one component of a composite endpoint does not necessarily translate into a beneficial effect on the other components of the composite endpoint.
, when interpreting the results of a clinical trial with a composite primary endpoint, the results should be interpreted separately for each component of the endpoint.
